name: Pale Orange
lede: Pale Orange is a light, soft orange, closer to a sherbet than to a fruit.

sections.title: Using it in color design
sections.body:
The name is descriptive, a lightened [[orange]] [3]. It is not a pigment name and the books we hold give it no history [3].

It does turn up in working color advice. Gurney describes a film color script in which each story unit sits inside a limited range of colors, or gamut [1]. When the adventure moves above ground, the gamut shifts to pale orange, yellow, pink and red [1]. The gamut changes with the story, so the same pale colors read as a mood and not just a swatch [1]. Neighbors in our data include [[peach]] and [[apricot]] [3].

The swatch on this page is #FFA756, the screen value we hold for it, which is an approximation and not a measured pigment [3]. Like any pale color it sits between its hue and [[white]], and because the name is a description and not a tradition, other lists may place it a little differently [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Pale Orange appears in 42 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 0.18 percent, as photographed [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, found in 8 of the 1,674 paintings from that century, about 2.2 times the museums' baseline rate [2].

origin.source: ColorHub library; Gurney, Color and Light, p. 134

choices: It shifts as the story moves
